title: Liam Rosenior: Enzo Fernandez row has not divided Chelsea squad
content:
Chelsea head coach Liam Rosenior says Enzo Fernandez’s fall-out with the club has not divided the dressing room and the midfielder is ready to face Manchester United on Saturday.

Fernandez was banned by Chelsea for two matches for making comments in the media about previous head coach Enzo Maresca’s departure from the club and for suggesting he was interested in a move to Real Madrid.

He returned to training this week after issuing an apology to Rosenior, the club’s hierarchy and after talking to his teammates.

While Rosenior has not confirmed if Fernandez will start against Manchester United, he insists the row has not caused any ongoing issues.

Pressed on whether the situation has split opinion among the players at all, he replied: “Not that I’m aware of, no. Enzo’s come back to the group this week. The group’s been fantastic in terms of his training, Enzo has as well. It’s just business as usual in terms of the selection for the game.”

Rosenior goes into the match under pressure with Chelsea having won just one of their last seven league outings. The run has left them closer to Bournemouth in 11th (three points) than to Liverpool in fifth (four points).

An organised fan protest against the ownership is also taking place before the game at Stamford Bridge.

Rosenior, who was manager of Hull City and Strasbourg before taking over Chelsea, admits it is a difficult period for him personally but is confident he can steer the team through its current difficulties.

Asked if this is his hardest moment as manager, he said: “Yeah, I think obviously we’re not in a good place in terms of the results. It’s a brilliant challenge in terms of myself, in terms of my energy, what I give the team, and more about what we do together.

“To be honest, every supporter has their viewpoint. Every supporter wants their club to do well and to win games of football. Our job, my job with the team, is to produce those results in the long term. I respect any fan’s points of view, but that’s (the protest) not my focus. My focus is on winning the game on Saturday.

“We’ve had a lot of really strong conversations as a group. We’ve had some very, very good training sessions. In this moment, you find out about yourself, you find out about your group, and you actually just have to stay focused on the process.

“We need to be perfect in every area or near perfect in every area to get to where we want to be (top five finish), but it’s possible.

“As the season goes on, the less games you have left, the more important the games become. We have to take advantage of this moment. We’re running out of time. We need to show that initiative on Saturday evening and we need to play on the front foot and we need to make up those points, which is still definitely possible.”

Defender Trevoh Chalobah has been in modified training after an ankle injury and a late decision will be made on whether he returns against Manchester United tomorrow.

Levi Colwill is playing for the Under-21s in a friendly tomorrow. he has not played since the Club World Cup final last July due to tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in pre-season.
